diagnostics.title: Share diagnostic data
diagnostics.description: Shares feature counts and time spent actively using Isoform to help us improve it. A random install ID links the counts; nothing you write, say or see is included. When this is off, no diagnostic data is sent.
diagnostics.detailsDescription: When sharing is on, Isoform records app opens, active foreground time, the first brief viewed, chat turns sent (count only), playbook runs, phone pairings and a daily active ping. A random install ID links these events without an account, name or email. Events include app version, flavor, OS version, language and telemetry tier; activity also includes a random session ID and duration. Five minutes without input ends active time. Never sent: screen text, audio, file names, URLs, people, memory, chat text or tool inputs and outputs. When sharing is off, nothing is queued or sent.

standalone.intro: Create your own Slack app, then paste its bot token and app token here. The setup steps under Advanced walk through each page.
standalone.step1: At api.slack.com/apps, click Create New App → From scratch, then name it and pick your workspace.
standalone.step2: Open Socket Mode (left sidebar) and turn on Enable Socket Mode. When prompted, generate an App-Level Token (scope connections:write) and copy it. This is your app token; it starts with xapp-.
standalone.step3: Open OAuth & Permissions → Scopes → Bot Token Scopes and add three scopes: app_mentions:read, chat:write, im:history.
standalone.step4: Open Event Subscriptions, turn on Enable Events (no Request URL is needed in Socket Mode), then under Subscribe to bot events add: app_mention and message.im.
standalone.step5: Open App Home, scroll to Show Tabs, turn on the Messages Tab, and check "Allow users to send Slash commands and messages from the messages tab". Otherwise direct messages to the bot are turned off.
standalone.step6: Open Install App, click Install to your workspace, and copy the Bot User OAuth Token. This is your bot token; it starts with xoxb-.
standalone.step7: Paste both tokens into the fields above and click Save and connect.
standalone.testOk: The token works (workspace {{team}}). Click Save and connect to finish.
standalone.stepsDescription: Each step is a page in your Slack app's settings. Isoform connects through Socket Mode, so the app needs no public web address.
standalone.pairHint: Send this code to the app in a direct message. Only the Slack account that sends it can use the app; messages from anyone else are ignored.

standalone.intro: Create your own Discord bot, paste its token here, then add it to your server. The setup steps under Advanced walk through the Developer Portal.
standalone.step1: At the Discord Developer Portal, create an application and a bot. Create it under your personal account, not a team. If you see "Missing Permissions", make sure you are using a personal account with a verified phone number.
standalone.step2: On the Bot page, enable the Message Content privileged intent, then Reset Token and copy it.
standalone.step3: Paste the bot token into the field above, then use the invite link to add the bot to your server.

It also reads the history of Chrome and other Chromium browsers on this computer (not Safari, never private windows), so the sites you visit most and what you searched for can appear in your brief. Password fields, private windows and the apps you ignore stay out. Turn this off if you would rather it never sees your screen.

listen.title: Listen
listen.descriptionWithSystemAudio: Isoform turns what you say into text all day, on this computer, and remembers what matters. Speech you dictate into another app, such as Claude or ChatGPT, is kept as dictation to that app (in a browser, while Record meetings automatically is on). With Record meetings automatically on, during a call it also hears the other side and keeps the call's audio. Outside calls no audio is kept, and the sound your computer plays is left out unless you turn it on below. Nothing said while a private browser window is in front becomes text, except in Safari, which does not mark its private windows.

reminders.description: Isoform reads the reminders on this computer, open and recently completed. Open ones count as your commitments, so it can tell you when one is due or overdue, and ticking one off closes it. Reminders are kept on this computer; open ones can appear in your brief on your paired phone, and what a task needs is sent to the AI you chose. Turning reading off stops new updates and keeps the reminders and commitments already saved on this computer. Revoking access in macOS removes the saved reminders and closes their commitments.

mail.title: Mail Isoform can see

Never the messages themselves, and Isoform never opens Mail. When someone you know wrote to you directly more than a day ago and has no answer yet, Isoform tells you. Mail headers stay on this computer; who is waiting and the subject can appear on your paired phone and in a notification on this computer, never in what is sent to the AI. Turning reading off or losing macOS access stops new collection and keeps the records already saved on this computer. Protecting Mail in Privacy deletes those records; a notification your phone already received stays there.

Nothing is noted from password managers, copies apps mark as passwords, private browser windows, Isoform itself or the apps you protect. Safari does not mark its private windows, so from Safari only the kind of copy is noted, never a preview.
